programme.displayName: Infrastructure as Code: AWS CloudFormation and Terraform Follow Along
programme.subtitle: Build, change, detect drift, reuse, compare, and safely remove AWS infrastructure with two IaC tools.
programme.description: Start with no lab infrastructure. Prepare temporary access, build equivalent low-cost AWS networks with CloudFormation and Terraform, protect Terraform state in versioned S3 with native lockfiles, practise change previews, drift, modules and import, compare both workflows, and complete an ordered teardown.
programme.learningOutcome: Create, review, update, troubleshoot, compare, and completely remove AWS infrastructure using CloudFormation and Terraform while protecting identity and state.

tasks.title: Prepare the administrator session and local tools
tasks.feature: IAM, AWS CLI, and Terraform CLI
tasks.goal: Verify the correct AWS account, select eu-west-2, install Terraform, and create separate CloudFormation and Terraform folders.
tasks.whyItMatters: IaC can change many resources at once, so identity, Region, versions, and file locations must be explicit before deployment.

tasks.title: Create the protected Terraform state bucket with CloudFormation
tasks.feature: CloudFormation, S3 encryption, versioning, and retention
tasks.goal: Deploy a bootstrap stack that creates one private, encrypted, versioned S3 state bucket.
tasks.whyItMatters: Terraform backends must exist before backend initialization, and state requires stronger protection than ordinary lab files.

consoleSteps.title: Deploy the backend stack
consoleSteps.instruction: Open CloudFormation in eu-west-2 and choose Create stack, With new resources.

instructions.text: Open CloudFormation in eu-west-2 and choose Create stack, With new resources.
Choose Upload a template file and upload the supplied fa-iac-backend.yaml.
Choose Next and enter stack name fa-iac-backend.
Review the template and keep the default options.
Choose Submit and watch the Events tab until CREATE_COMPLETE.
Open Outputs and record StateBucketName as [TF_STATE_BUCKET].
Open the S3 bucket and verify Block Public Access, SSE-S3 default encryption, and versioning are enabled.

jsonBlocks.title: fa-iac-backend.yaml
jsonBlocks.content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Versioned encrypted S3 backend for the fa-iac Terraform lab
Resources:
  StateBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Join ['', ['fa-iac-tf-state-', !Ref 'AWS::AccountId']]
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: AES256
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
Outputs:
  StateBucketName:
    Value: !Ref StateBucket

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-iac-backend is CREATE_COMPLETE and [TF_STATE_BUCKET] is protected.
consoleSteps.warning: The template retains the bucket when the stack is deleted so state cannot disappear accidentally.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation validate-template --template-body file://fa-iac-backend.yaml --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Validate the visible backend template.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns the template description.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation deploy --stack-name fa-iac-backend --template-file fa-iac-backend.yaml --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Create or safely update the backend stack.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The deployment succeeds.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name fa-iac-backend --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Read the stack output.
cliSteps.expectedResult: StateBucketName provides [TF_STATE_BUCKET].

verification.title: Verify backend controls
verification.instruction: Inspect the S3 bucket Properties and Permissions tabs.
verification.expectedResult: Versioning and encryption are enabled and public access is blocked.

tasks.title: Build and deploy a CloudFormation network stack
tasks.feature: CloudFormation templates, parameters, resources, and outputs
tasks.goal: Create a VPC, subnet, and no-ingress security group from the supplied YAML template.
tasks.whyItMatters: The stack demonstrates declarative dependencies, intrinsic functions, tags, and outputs without expensive compute resources.

consoleSteps.title: Create the workload stack
consoleSteps.instruction: Open CloudFormation in eu-west-2 and choose Create stack, With new resources.

instructions.text: Open CloudFormation in eu-west-2 and choose Create stack, With new resources.
Upload the supplied fa-iac-network.yaml.
Enter stack name fa-iac-cfn-network.
On Parameters, keep EnvironmentName as fa-iac-cfn.
Review the template summary and choose Submit.
Follow Events from the oldest event upward and wait for CREATE_COMPLETE.
Open Resources and identify the VPC, subnet, and security group physical IDs.
Open Outputs and record [CFN_VPC_ID], [CFN_SUBNET_ID], and [CFN_SG_ID].
Open VPC and verify the resources have ManagedBy = CloudFormation.

jsonBlocks.title: fa-iac-network.yaml
jsonBlocks.content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: CloudFormation half of the fa-iac comparison lab
Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: fa-iac-cfn
Resources:
  VPC:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.30.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ['', [!Ref EnvironmentName, '-vpc']]
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation
  PublicSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      CidrBlock: 10.30.1.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ['', [!Ref EnvironmentName, '-subnet']]
  SecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: No-ingress comparison security group
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      SecurityGroupEgress:
        - IpProtocol: '-1'
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ['', [!Ref EnvironmentName, '-sg']]
Outputs:
  VpcId:
    Value: !Ref VPC
  SubnetId:
    Value: !Ref PublicSubnet
  SecurityGroupId:
    Value: !Ref SecurityGroup

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The three network resources exist in 10.30.0.0/16 and the stack is CREATE_COMPLETE.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation validate-template --template-body file://fa-iac-network.yaml --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Check YAML structure before deployment.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The template description and parameter are returned.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation deploy --stack-name fa-iac-cfn-network --template-file fa-iac-network.yaml --parameter-overrides EnvironmentName=fa-iac-cfn --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Deploy the network stack.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The stack deployment succeeds.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name fa-iac-cfn-network --query "Stacks[0].Outputs" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Retrieve the generated resource IDs.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Three outputs are returned.

tasks.title: Preview and execute a CloudFormation change set
tasks.goal: Change the subnet Name tag through a reviewed change set and understand rollback events.
tasks.whyItMatters: Change sets expose intended replacements or modifications before they affect the environment.

consoleSteps.title: Create and inspect the change set

instructions.text: Make a copy named fa-iac-network-v2.yaml.
In the copy, change only the PublicSubnet Name value to fa-iac-cfn-subnet-v2.
Open fa-iac-cfn-network and choose Stack actions, Create change set for current stack.
Upload fa-iac-network-v2.yaml and name the change set fa-iac-subnet-tag-change.
Wait for CREATE_COMPLETE and inspect every proposed resource action.
Confirm the subnet action is Modify and Replacement is False.
Execute the change set and watch Events until UPDATE_COMPLETE.
Open the subnet Tags and verify Name = fa-iac-cfn-subnet-v2.
Open stack Events and identify the UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS and UPDATE_COMPLETE sequence.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The reviewed tag-only change is applied without replacing the subnet.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation create-change-set --stack-name fa-iac-cfn-network --change-set-name fa-iac-subnet-tag-change --template-body file://fa-iac-network-v2.yaml --parameters ParameterKey=EnvironmentName,UsePreviousValue=true --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Create a non-executing preview of the update.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A change set ID is returned.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation describe-change-set --stack-name fa-iac-cfn-network --change-set-name fa-iac-subnet-tag-change --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Review the exact proposed action and replacement status.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The subnet shows Modify with no replacement.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation execute-change-set --stack-name fa-iac-cfn-network --change-set-name fa-iac-subnet-tag-change --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Apply only the reviewed change set.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The stack begins updating.

verification.title: Verify non-replacement update
verification.instruction: Compare [CFN_SUBNET_ID] before and after the update.
verification.expectedResult: The physical subnet ID is unchanged and only its Name tag differs.

tasks.title: Detect and reconcile CloudFormation drift
tasks.goal: Create one harmless tag drift, detect it, and restore the template-defined value.
tasks.whyItMatters: Drift reveals changes made outside the IaC control plane and is a common governance concern.

consoleSteps.title: Create, detect, and remove controlled drift
consoleSteps.instruction: Open VPC, select [CFN_VPC_ID], and add temporary tag DriftTest = manual-change.

instructions.text: Open VPC, select [CFN_VPC_ID], and add temporary tag DriftTest = manual-change.
Return to CloudFormation and open fa-iac-cfn-network.
Choose Stack actions, Detect drift, then confirm.
Wait for DRIFTED and open View drift results.
Select the VPC resource and compare expected with actual properties.
Remove only the DriftTest tag in the VPC console.
Run Detect drift again.
Wait until the stack returns to IN_SYNC.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudFormation first reports the controlled difference and then reports IN_SYNC.
consoleSteps.warning: Change only the named DriftTest tag; do not edit CIDRs or delete resources.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudformation detect-stack-drift --stack-name fa-iac-cfn-network --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-iac
cliSteps.explanation: Start drift detection.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record StackDriftDetectionId.

cliSteps.explanation: Read the detection result.
cliSteps.expectedResult: DetectionStatus is DETECTION_COMPLETE and StackDriftStatus reflects the current state.

verification.title: Verify reconciliation
verification.instruction: Run drift detection after removing the tag.

tasks.whyItMatters: Remote state supports collaboration and recovery; locking reduces concurrent-write risk.

tasks.title: Practise Terraform drift and import decisions safely
tasks.feature: Terraform refresh, plan, import, and state ownership
tasks.goal: Observe one harmless tag drift and practise the import workflow using a separate unmanaged security group.
tasks.whyItMatters: Terraform plans reconcile real infrastructure with configuration, while import adopts existing resources without creating them.

consoleSteps.title: Detect drift and prepare an import target
consoleSteps.instruction: In VPC, add DriftTest = manual-change to fa-iac-tf-subnet only.

instructions.text: In VPC, add DriftTest = manual-change to fa-iac-tf-subnet only.
Run terraform plan and find the proposed removal of DriftTest.
Remove the manual tag in the Console and run terraform plan again.
Create a no-ingress security group named fa-iac-import-sg in fa-iac-tf-vpc.
Record its ID as [IMPORT_SG_ID].
Add an aws_security_group.imported resource block matching its name, description, VPC, egress, and tags.
Run terraform import aws_security_group.imported [IMPORT_SG_ID].
Run terraform plan and adjust configuration until no unexpected changes remain.
Keep the imported security group in configuration so terraform destroy can remove it.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Drift is visible in a plan, and the existing security group becomes managed without recreation.
consoleSteps.warning: Import does not generate complete configuration. Match the real object before applying.

cliSteps.expectedResult: The plan proposes removing only DriftTest.

cliSteps.explanation: Attach the existing security group to the declared resource address.

tasks.title: Compare IaC workflows and complete the teardown
tasks.goal: Compare both tools, then remove Terraform workloads, CloudFormation workloads, backend objects, backend stack, and temporary access in exact order.
tasks.whyItMatters: The owning IaC tool should remove its own resources, and retained state must be handled only after the managed workload is gone.

consoleSteps.title: Compare before deleting

instructions.text: Open CloudFormation Resources for fa-iac-cfn-network.
Open VPC and filter ManagedBy = CloudFormation, then ManagedBy = Terraform.
Compare template plus stack events with HCL plus plan and state.
Record that CloudFormation state is service-managed while Terraform state is stored in [TF_STATE_BUCKET].
Choose CloudFormation when AWS-native service integration and stack operations fit the requirement.
Choose Terraform when a shared declarative workflow across supported providers and reusable modules fits the requirement.
Confirm all recorded IDs belong to this lab before cleanup.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner can explain ownership, preview, state, drift, reuse, and cleanup differences.

consoleSteps.title: Run the final deletion order
consoleSteps.instruction: From fa-iac/terraform, run terraform plan -destroy and confirm only fa-iac-tf resources are listed.

instructions.text: From fa-iac/terraform, run terraform plan -destroy and confirm only fa-iac-tf resources are listed.
Run terraform destroy and type yes only after checking every address.
Verify fa-iac-tf-vpc, subnet, and both security groups are absent.
Delete CloudFormation stack fa-iac-cfn-network and wait for DELETE_COMPLETE.
Verify fa-iac-cfn resources are absent.
In [TF_STATE_BUCKET], delete every version and delete marker only under cloudformation-terraform/terraform.tfstate and its .tflock key.
Delete CloudFormation stack fa-iac-backend; the bucket is retained intentionally.
After the backend stack is deleted, empty all remaining versions and delete markers from [TF_STATE_BUCKET].
Delete the empty [TF_STATE_BUCKET].
Delete the fa-iac access key, detach and delete fa-iac-training-policy, and delete fa-iac-user.
Remove only the local fa-iac AWS CLI profile and local fa-iac working folder.
